title: 1 Samuel Chapter 2 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on 1 Samuel chapter 2 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: 1 Samuel Chapter 2 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of 1 Samuel Chapter 2.

questions.question: Who prayed and said, 'My heart rejoiceth in the LORD' in 1 Samuel 2?
options: Hannah
Elkanah
Eli
Samuel
questions.correctAnswer: Hannah
questions.explanation: Hannah prayed and said these words, as stated in 1 Samuel 2:1.

questions.question: According to 1 Samuel 2:2, what is said to be unique about the LORD?
options: There is none holy as the LORD
The LORD is like any other god
The LORD is one among many rocks
The LORD speaks through priests only
questions.correctAnswer: There is none holy as the LORD
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 2:2 states that there is none holy as the LORD and no rock like our God.

questions.question: What does 1 Samuel 2:3 warn against in speech?
options: Talking too quietly
Speaking proudly and arrogantly
Using foreign languages
Singing before the LORD
questions.correctAnswer: Speaking proudly and arrogantly
questions.explanation: Verse 3 warns against speaking with arrogance or pride, as the LORD is a God of knowledge who weighs actions.

questions.question: What happens to the bows of the mighty men according to 1 Samuel 2:4?
options: They are strengthened
They are broken
They are made new
They are ignored
questions.correctAnswer: They are broken
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 2:4 says the bows of the mighty men are broken, while those who stumbled are girded with strength.

questions.question: According to 1 Samuel 2:5, what unusual circumstance is mentioned about the barren woman?
options: She bore seven children
She remained childless
She fled to the mountains
She hired servants
questions.correctAnswer: She bore seven children
questions.explanation: Verse 5 states that the barren woman has born seven children, contrasting with others who are feeble.

questions.question: True or False: 1 Samuel 2:6 says the LORD only brings life and does not bring death.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 2:6 states the LORD killeth and maketh alive, so He brings both death and life.

questions.question: What does the LORD do according to 1 Samuel 2:7?
options: Only blesses the wealthy
Maketh poor and rich; bringeth low and lifteth up
Remains neutral to all people
Only punishes sinners
questions.correctAnswer: Maketh poor and rich; bringeth low and lifteth up
questions.explanation: Verse 7 clearly states the LORD maketh poor and rich, and bringeth low and lifteth up.

questions.question: In 1 Samuel 2:8, from where does the LORD raise up the poor and beggar?
options: From the mountains
Out of the dust and the dunghill
From the sea
From the city gates
questions.correctAnswer: Out of the dust and the dunghill
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 2:8 says He raiseth up the poor out of the dust and lifteth up the beggar from the dunghill.

questions.question: According to 1 Samuel 2:9, what will happen to the wicked?
options: They will prosper
They shall be silent in darkness
They will be exalted
They will judge the saints
questions.correctAnswer: They shall be silent in darkness
questions.explanation: Verse 9 states that the wicked shall be silent in darkness because by strength no man shall prevail.

questions.question: What shall the LORD do to His adversaries as stated in 1 Samuel 2:10?
options: Bless them
Break them to pieces
Ignore them
Make them priests
questions.correctAnswer: Break them to pieces
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 2:10 says the adversaries of the LORD shall be broken to pieces and thundered upon from heaven.

questions.question: Where did Elkanah go after the events described in the earlier verses of 1 Samuel 2?
options: Shiloh
Ramah
Bethel
Jerusalem
questions.correctAnswer: Ramah
questions.explanation: Verse 11 states Elkanah went to Ramah to his house after the events.

questions.question: True or False: According to 1 Samuel 2:12, Eli's sons were known to be righteous and faithful to the LORD.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Verse 12 states the sons of Eli were sons of Belial and knew not the LORD, indicating unrighteousness.

questions.question: According to 1 Samuel 2:1-10, what comes FIRST in Hannah’s prayer?
options: The LORD maketh poor, and maketh rich
My heart rejoiceth in the LORD
The adversaries of the LORD shall be broken
There is none holy as the LORD
questions.correctAnswer: My heart rejoiceth in the LORD
questions.explanation: In verse 1, Hannah begins her prayer by saying, 'My heart rejoiceth in the LORD,' which comes before other statements in the chapter.

questions.question: True or False: 1 Samuel 2:4 mentions that those who stumbled are girded with strength.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Verse 4 states that those who stumbled are girded with strength, confirming the truth of this statement.

questions.question: True or False: According to 1 Samuel 2:9, by strength alone shall man prevail.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Verse 9 clearly says, 'for by strength shall no man prevail,' showing that strength alone is insufficient.

medium.title: 1 Samuel Chapter 2 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from 1 Samuel Chapter 2 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What was the custom of the priests' servants when a man offered a sacrifice, according to 1 Samuel 2?
options: They waited until the sacrifice was fully burned before taking any portion
They took the flesh while it was boiling using a fleshhook of three teeth
They refused to take any portion of the sacrifice
They asked the offerer to give them a portion of bread
questions.correctAnswer: They took the flesh while it was boiling using a fleshhook of three teeth
questions.explanation: Verses 13 and 14 describe that the priests' servants came with a fleshhook of three teeth while the flesh was seething and took it for themselves, showing a corrupt practice.

questions.question: According to 1 Samuel 2, what did the priest's servant demand before the fat was burned?
options: That the fat be burned immediately
That the man offer a payment in silver
Raw flesh to roast for the priest
That the offering be shared equally
questions.correctAnswer: Raw flesh to roast for the priest
questions.explanation: Verse 15 states the priest's servant said to the man sacrificing, 'Give flesh to roast for the priest; for he will not have sodden flesh of thee, but raw,' indicating a demand for raw meat.

questions.question: What does 1 Samuel 2:16 reveal about the behavior of the priest's servant when challenged about taking portions of the sacrifice?
options: He would politely wait for the fat to be burned before taking any
He insisted on taking the portion immediately and threatened force if refused
He allowed the offerer to decide when to give the portion
He gave the portion back to the offerer
questions.correctAnswer: He insisted on taking the portion immediately and threatened force if refused
questions.explanation: Verse 16 explains that the servant would not accept delay and said, 'Nay; but thou shalt give it me now: and if not, I will take it by force,' showing his arrogance and corruption.

questions.question: What was the consequence of the young men’s sinful behavior before the LORD as described in this chapter?
options: The people rejoiced in their leadership
The offering of the LORD was abhorred by men
They were rewarded with blessings
They were promoted to higher priestly offices
questions.correctAnswer: The offering of the LORD was abhorred by men
questions.explanation: Verse 17 states that the sin of the young men was very great before the LORD and as a result, men abhorred the offering of the LORD, showing the negative impact of their behavior.

questions.question: How did Samuel serve the LORD as a child according to this chapter?
options: He led the people in sacrifices
He ministered before the LORD, girded with a linen ephod
He taught the law to the children
He went out as a prophet to the nations
questions.correctAnswer: He ministered before the LORD, girded with a linen ephod
questions.explanation: Verse 18 describes that Samuel ministered before the LORD as a child, wearing a linen ephod, indicating his early dedication and service.

questions.question: What did Samuel’s mother do for him yearly when she came up with her husband to offer the yearly sacrifice?
options: She brought him a lamb to sacrifice
She made him a little coat
She offered a special prayer
She taught him the Scriptures
questions.correctAnswer: She made him a little coat
questions.explanation: Verse 19 says that Samuel’s mother made him a little coat and brought it to him yearly when they came to offer the yearly sacrifice, showing her care and support.

questions.question: What blessing did Eli pronounce on Elkanah and his wife?
options: That they would become wealthy merchants
That the LORD give them seed for the loan lent to the LORD
That they would be priests in the tabernacle
That they would have peace in the land
questions.correctAnswer: That the LORD give them seed for the loan lent to the LORD
questions.explanation: Verse 20 records Eli blessing Elkanah and his wife, praying that the LORD would give them children as a seed in return for the child lent to the LORD, referring to Samuel.

questions.question: How did the LORD respond to Hannah according to this chapter?
options: He ignored her prayers
He visited her so she conceived and bore children
He commanded her to leave the tabernacle
He punished her for her impatience
questions.correctAnswer: He visited her so she conceived and bore children
questions.explanation: Verse 21 states that the LORD visited Hannah, causing her to conceive and bear three sons and two daughters, showing God's faithfulness to her prayer.

questions.question: What did Eli, being very old, hear about his sons’ behavior?
options: That they were faithful priests
That they lay with the women who assembled at the tabernacle door
That they led the people in worship
That they were humble and obedient
questions.correctAnswer: That they lay with the women who assembled at the tabernacle door
questions.explanation: Verse 22 reports that Eli heard how his sons lay with the women who came to the tabernacle door, indicating their immoral behavior.

questions.question: What was Eli’s reaction when he heard about his sons’ evil dealings?
options: He praised them for their leadership
He rebuked them and warned about the consequences
He ignored the reports
He expelled them from the tabernacle immediately
questions.correctAnswer: He rebuked them and warned about the consequences
questions.explanation: Verses 23-24 show Eli asking his sons why they did such things and telling them the report is not good because they cause the LORD’S people to transgress.

questions.question: According to 1 Samuel 2, what does Eli say about sinning against the LORD compared to sinning against another person?
options: Sinning against the LORD can be easily forgiven
If a man sins against the LORD, who will intercede for him?
Sin against a person is worse than sin against the LORD
The priests will always intercede for those who sin
questions.correctAnswer: If a man sins against the LORD, who will intercede for him?
questions.explanation: Verse 25 explains that if one sins against another, a judge will judge him, but if one sins against the LORD, there is no intercessor, emphasizing the seriousness of sin against God.

questions.question: What does 1 Samuel 2 teach about the growth of Samuel during this time?
options: He grew only in physical stature
He grew in favor with both the LORD and men
He grew distant from the people
He stopped ministering in the tabernacle
questions.correctAnswer: He grew in favor with both the LORD and men
questions.explanation: Verse 26 states that Samuel grew and was favored both by the LORD and by people, highlighting his spiritual and social growth.

questions.question: True or False: The priests’ sons honored the LORD and served Him faithfully.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Verse 12 declares that the sons of Eli were sons of Belial and did not know the LORD, indicating their unfaithfulness.

questions.question: True or False: Eli warned his sons to stop their sinful behavior because it caused the LORD's people to transgress.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Verses 23-24 record Eli rebuking his sons for their evil deeds and stating that their behavior causes the LORD’s people to transgress, showing his warning.

questions.question: True or False: According to 1 Samuel 2, the LORD will honor those who despise Him.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Verse 30 states that those who honor the LORD will be honored, and those who despise Him shall be lightly esteemed, so the statement is false.

hard.title: 1 Samuel Chapter 2 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from 1 Samuel Chapter 2.

questions.question: According to 1 Samuel 2:25, what is the consequence of sinning against the LORD compared to sinning against a man?
options: The judge will intercede for the man who sinned against the LORD
No one can intercede for a man who sins against the LORD
The man will be forgiven instantly if he repents
The sin against the LORD is less serious than against a man
questions.correctAnswer: No one can intercede for a man who sins against the LORD
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 2:25 states that if a man sins against another, the judge will judge him, but if a man sins against the LORD, no one can intercede for him. This highlights the severity of sinning against God.

questions.question: What is said about Samuel in 1 Samuel 2:26?
options: He was rejected by both men and God
He was favored by both the LORD and men
He was only favored by men but not by God
He was a rebellious child
questions.correctAnswer: He was favored by both the LORD and men
questions.explanation: The verse 1 Samuel 2:26 states that Samuel grew and was in favor both with the LORD and also with men, indicating his favorable status in both divine and human eyes.

questions.question: In 1 Samuel 2:27-28, what question does the man of God ask Eli about his priestly heritage?
options: Did God choose Eli's family to be kings of Israel?
Did God appear to Eli's ancestors in Egypt and appoint them priests?
Did Eli's family build the tabernacle in Egypt?
Did Eli's sons follow God's commandments perfectly?
questions.correctAnswer: Did God appear to Eli's ancestors in Egypt and appoint them priests?
questions.explanation: The man of God questions Eli if God appeared to his father's house in Egypt and chose them to be priests, as stated in 1 Samuel 2:27-28, challenging Eli's family's legitimacy.

questions.question: What is the reason given in 1 Samuel 2:29 for God's judgment against Eli's house?
options: They neglected the temple building
They honored their sons over God and misused offerings
They refused to offer sacrifices
They worshiped idols secretly
questions.correctAnswer: They honored their sons over God and misused offerings
questions.explanation: Verse 29 explains that Eli's house was judged because they honored their sons above God and made themselves fat with the chief offerings, showing corruption and disrespect for God's commands.

questions.question: According to 1 Samuel 2:30, what promise does the LORD make regarding those who honor and despise Him?
options: Those who honor God will be dishonored, and those who despise Him will be honored
Those who honor God will be honored, and those who despise Him will be lightly esteemed
All will be treated equally regardless of their attitude toward God
Those who despise God will be destroyed immediately
questions.correctAnswer: Those who honor God will be honored, and those who despise Him will be lightly esteemed
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 2:30 promises that God will honor those who honor Him and lightly esteem those who despise Him, emphasizing the importance of reverence toward God.

questions.question: What specific punishment does God declare in 1 Samuel 2:31-32 for Eli's house?
options: They will be blessed with many descendants
There will be no old men left in Eli's house, and an enemy will enter God's habitation
They will become kings of Israel
They will inherit the land of Canaan
questions.correctAnswer: There will be no old men left in Eli's house, and an enemy will enter God's habitation
questions.explanation: Verses 31-32 declare that God will cut off the strength of Eli's house so that no old man remains, and an enemy will come into His habitation, indicating severe judgment.

questions.question: According to 1 Samuel 2:33, what will happen to the man of Eli's house who is not cut off from the altar?
options: He will become the high priest
He will consume Eli’s eyes and grieve his heart
He will be exalted above others
He will prosper and live long
questions.correctAnswer: He will consume Eli’s eyes and grieve his heart
questions.explanation: Verse 33 states that the man of Eli's house who remains at the altar will bring grief and consume his eyes, symbolizing deep sorrow and loss within Eli's family.

questions.question: What sign does God give Eli about the fate of his two sons in 1 Samuel 2:34?
options: They will become kings of Israel
They will die on the same day
They will build a new temple
They will be taken captive to Egypt
questions.correctAnswer: They will die on the same day
questions.explanation: Verse 34 gives the sign that both Hophni and Phinehas, Eli's two sons, will die on the same day, foretelling their sudden death as judgment.

questions.question: What future priest does God promise to raise up in 1 Samuel 2:35?
options: A priest who will rebel against God
A faithful priest who will do according to God’s heart and mind
A priest from another nation
A priest who will not walk before the anointed
questions.correctAnswer: A faithful priest who will do according to God’s heart and mind
questions.explanation: Verse 35 promises a faithful priest will be raised who acts according to God's will and walks before the anointed forever, foreshadowing a righteous priestly line.

questions.question: In 1 Samuel 2:36, what will those left in Eli’s house have to do?
options: Become kings of Israel
Crouch to the faithful priest for a piece of silver and bread
Lead the people in worship
Be priests themselves without permission
questions.correctAnswer: Crouch to the faithful priest for a piece of silver and bread
questions.explanation: Verse 36 states that those left in Eli's house will have to humble themselves and ask the faithful priest for a piece of silver and bread, indicating a loss of status and dependence.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage echoes the theme of a faithful priest raised by God as mentioned in 1 Samuel 2:35?
options: Psalm 110:4
Genesis 1:1
Exodus 20:1
Revelation 21:1
questions.correctAnswer: Psalm 110:4
questions.explanation: Psalm 110:4 speaks of a priest forever after the order of Melchizedek, echoing the theme of a faithful priest raised by God as in 1 Samuel 2:35.

questions.question: What is the Hebrew meaning of the word 'ephod' mentioned in 1 Samuel 2:18 and 2:28, and what is its significance?
options: A garment worn by kings symbolizing authority
A linen priestly garment used as a symbol of priestly office
A type of ancient weapon
A ceremonial crown worn by prophets
questions.correctAnswer: A linen priestly garment used as a symbol of priestly office
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word 'ephod' refers to a linen garment worn by priests, symbolizing their office and role before the LORD, as seen in 1 Samuel 2:18 and 2:28.

questions.question: What literary device is prominently used in Hannah’s prayer in 1 Samuel 2:1-10?
options: Chiasm
Simile
Parable
Hyperbole
questions.correctAnswer: Chiasm
questions.explanation: Hannah’s prayer in 1 Samuel 2:1-10 uses chiasm, a literary device where ideas are presented and then repeated in reverse order, highlighting the reversal of fortunes and God's sovereignty.

questions.question: True or False: According to 1 Samuel 2:12, the sons of Eli were righteous and knew the LORD well.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 2:12 explicitly states that the sons of Eli were sons of Belial and knew not the LORD, indicating their unrighteousness and ignorance of God.

questions.question: True or False: According to 1 Samuel 2:26, Samuel was favored both by the LORD and by men as he grew.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 2:26 clearly states that Samuel grew on and was in favor with both the LORD and also with men, confirming the truth of the statement.

theological.title: 1 Samuel Chapter 2 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from 1 Samuel Chapter 2 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is primarily highlighted in Hannah's prayer when she says, 'There is none holy as the LORD'?
options: Holiness
Omniscience
Omnipotence
Mercy
questions.correctAnswer: Holiness
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 2:2 emphasizes God's holiness by stating 'There is none holy as the LORD', declaring His unique and absolute purity.

questions.question: What theological truth about divine justice is taught in 1 Samuel 2:3 regarding the LORD's knowledge and judgment?
options: The LORD is unaware of human actions
Human actions are judged by human standards
The LORD is a God of knowledge and weighs actions
Pride is rewarded by God
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD is a God of knowledge and weighs actions
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 2:3 states that 'the LORD is a God of knowledge, and by him actions are weighed', affirming God's perfect understanding and just judgment.

questions.question: According to 1 Samuel 2:6, what two sovereign powers does the LORD exercise over life and death?
options: He creates and destroys
He kills and makes alive; brings down to the grave and brings up
He judges and saves
He blesses and curses
questions.correctAnswer: He kills and makes alive; brings down to the grave and brings up
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 2:6 reveals God's sovereignty over life and death by saying 'The LORD killeth, and maketh alive: he bringeth down to the grave, and bringeth up'.

questions.question: What does 1 Samuel 2:7 teach about God's sovereignty in terms of human prosperity and adversity?
options: God only blesses the righteous
God maketh poor, and maketh rich; he bringeth low, and lifteth up
Humans control their own wealth
Prosperity is a sign of God's favor
questions.correctAnswer: God maketh poor, and maketh rich; he bringeth low, and lifteth up
questions.explanation: This verse teaches God's absolute sovereignty in bestowing wealth or poverty, raising or lowering individuals according to His will (1 Samuel 2:7).

questions.question: How does 1 Samuel 2:8 express God's care for the lowly and outcast in relation to His cosmic authority?
options: God ignores the poor
God raises the poor from dust and sets them among princes, as He is the foundation of the earth
The poor are left to their own devices
Only kings have God's favor
questions.correctAnswer: God raises the poor from dust and sets them among princes, as He is the foundation of the earth
questions.explanation: Verse 8 shows God's care by raising the lowly 'out of the dust' and placing them in positions of honor, reflecting His sovereign cosmic authority as 'the pillars of the earth are the LORD'S'.

questions.question: What does 1 Samuel 2:9 teach about the ultimate fate of the wicked and the security of the saints?
options: The wicked will triumph and the saints will fall
God will keep the feet of his saints; the wicked shall be silent in darkness
Both wicked and saints are equal in God's sight
The wicked will be rewarded
questions.correctAnswer: God will keep the feet of his saints; the wicked shall be silent in darkness
questions.explanation: This verse declares God's protection over the saints and the defeat and silence of the wicked, affirming divine justice (1 Samuel 2:9).

questions.question: Which future Messianic promise is found in 1 Samuel 2:10 concerning the LORD's anointed king?
options: The LORD will reject his anointed
The LORD will give strength to his king and exalt the horn of his anointed
The king will fail in battle
The anointed will be forgotten
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD will give strength to his king and exalt the horn of his anointed
questions.explanation: Verse 10 prophesies the divine strengthening and exaltation of God's anointed king, foreshadowing the Messiah.

questions.question: What doctrine regarding priestly corruption is illustrated by the behavior of Eli’s sons in verses 12 to 17?
options: The priesthood is infallible
Priests can sin and cause people to abhor offerings
Only laypeople sin, not priests
Sin in the priesthood has no effect on the people
questions.correctAnswer: Priests can sin and cause people to abhor offerings
questions.explanation: The sons of Eli are described as 'sons of Belial' whose sins caused people to abhor the LORD's offerings (1 Samuel 2:12–17), teaching that priestly sin leads to communal defilement.

questions.question: How does 1 Samuel 2:18 show Samuel's early role in contrast to the corrupt priesthood?
options: Samuel ministered before the LORD as a child, showing faithful service
Samuel was corrupt like Eli's sons
Samuel rejected the priesthood
Samuel was indifferent to the LORD
questions.correctAnswer: Samuel ministered before the LORD as a child, showing faithful service
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 2:18 presents Samuel as a faithful child ministering before the LORD, contrasting the corrupt behavior of Eli’s sons and foreshadowing renewal.

questions.question: What does the divine judgment pronounced in 1 Samuel 2:27-34 reveal about God’s holiness and justice in response to priestly sin?
options: God ignores sin in the priesthood
God will cut off the house of Eli because of their dishonor and corruption
God rewards the corrupt priests
God will let Eli's house continue forever
questions.correctAnswer: God will cut off the house of Eli because of their dishonor and corruption
questions.explanation: Verses 27-34 show God's just judgment against Eli’s house for their dishonoring Him and abusing sacrifices, revealing His holiness and intolerance of sin in leadership.

questions.question: Synthesis: What combined theological insight about God's sovereign choice and judgment emerges from 1 Samuel 2:28 and 1 Samuel 2:30?
options: God chooses and honors those who despise Him
God has chosen the house of Eli forever without judgment
God chooses His priests and honors those who honor Him, but despises those who reject Him
Human choice overrides God's election
questions.correctAnswer: God chooses His priests and honors those who honor Him, but despises those who reject Him
questions.explanation: Verse 28 shows God's choosing of priestly service, while verse 30 states God honors those who honor Him and lightly esteems those who despise Him, teaching sovereign election and just judgment.

questions.question: Synthesis: How do 1 Samuel 2:5 and 1 Samuel 2:7 together illustrate the doctrine of God's providential control over human circumstances?
options: God is indifferent to human fortune
God providentially reverses human conditions, making the barren fruitful and lifting up the lowly
Human effort alone determines prosperity
God only blesses the wealthy
questions.correctAnswer: God providentially reverses human conditions, making the barren fruitful and lifting up the lowly
questions.explanation: Verse 5 shows barren women bearing children and the full becoming hungry, and verse 7 states God makes poor or rich, illustrating His providence over human states.

questions.question: Synthesis: What combined teaching about the consequences of sin and parental authority is found in 1 Samuel 2:23-25 and 1 Samuel 2:34?
options: Sin has no consequences for families
Parental warning is sufficient to prevent sin
Sin against the LORD leads to divine judgment despite parental admonition, as shown in the death of Hophni and Phinehas
God excuses the sons because of Eli's warnings
questions.correctAnswer: Sin against the LORD leads to divine judgment despite parental admonition, as shown in the death of Hophni and Phinehas
questions.explanation: Eli's sons sinned despite his warnings (vv. 23-25), and verse 34 prophesies their death as judgment, showing sin against God brings serious consequences.

questions.question: Narrative arc: How does Samuel’s growth in favor with both God and men in 1 Samuel 2:26 contribute to the overarching redemptive narrative of Scripture?
options: It shows Samuel as a failed leader
It introduces Samuel as a faithful servant foreshadowing the coming Messiah
It suggests Samuel will be ignored by God
It indicates Samuel was corrupt like Eli's sons
questions.correctAnswer: It introduces Samuel as a faithful servant foreshadowing the coming Messiah
questions.explanation: Samuel's growth in favor (v. 26) sets him as a pivotal faithful figure in Israel's history, pointing forward to Christ’s ultimate faithful priesthood.

questions.question: Narrative arc: What role does 1 Samuel 2:35 assign to the faithful priest God will raise up, and how does this anticipate New Testament Christology?
options: The priest will be a political leader only
The faithful priest will act according to God's heart and establish an eternal house, foreshadowing Christ's eternal priesthood
The priest will be a temporary figure
The priest will be rejected by God
questions.correctAnswer: The faithful priest will act according to God's heart and establish an eternal house, foreshadowing Christ's eternal priesthood
questions.explanation: Verse 35 promises God will raise a faithful priest who aligns with God's heart and establishes an eternal house, a clear type of Christ's eternal priesthood (Hebrews 7:24-25).
